                                                                              at
NOTE:
                                                                            D
The calculation of the stability curve and the metacentric height, GM, take the actual floating
position into account. Therefore small deviation to manual calculations can NOT be prevented:


                                                                        74
The real free surface moment is calculated for the tanks at their actual filling. The correction
for different heeling angles is got by calculating the real new center of gravity for the load in
the heeled tank. The correction for the initial GM is got by calculating the real moment of
inertia for the free surface in the tank.
                                                                       91
In addition, according to regulations for stability calculations, some free surface moments may be

                                                                 49
assumed more conservative, and therefore final GM may differ from the one calculated manually.

6 INSTRUCTIONS FOR MASTER
                                                                                                                      01
6.1 GENERAL
                                                                                                               -2
                                                                                                         PR
COMPLIANCE WITH THE STABILITY CRITERIA DOES NOT ENSURE IMMUNITY AGAINST CAPSIZING, REGARDLESS OF THE CIRCUMSTANCES,
OR ABSOLVE THE MASTER FROM HIS RESPONSIBILITIES.
Master should therefore exercise prudence and good seamanship, having regard to the season of year, weather


                                                                                                    -A
forecasts and the navigational zone, and should take the appropriate action as to speed and course warranted by
the prevailing circumstances.



                                                                                               04
Care should be taken to ensure that the cargo allocated to the ship is capable of being stowed, so that
compliance with the criteria can be achieved. If necessary, the amount should be limited to the extent that
ballast weight may be required.



                                                                                         ed
Before a voyage commences, care should be taken to ensure that the cargo and sizeable pieces of equipment have
been properly stowed or lashed, so as to minimize the possibility of both longitudinal and lateral shifting while
at sea, under the effect of acceleration caused by rolling and pitching.


                                                                                     at
It is important to ensure that all ballast tanks in any condition, which are to be full, are in fact pressed
full. Those tanks which are dry should be completely dry.

                                                                                 D
When a tank is to be ballasted at sea to counteract the loss of consumables, it should be noted that:


- The tank will have a complete free surface as ballasting commences.
                                                                           74
- The free surface will adversely effect the stability of the vessel before any benefit can be assumed by the
weight of the ballast water taken on board.



6.2 PRINCIPLES FOR STABILITY
                                                                      91
                                                                 49
The loading conditions in this booklet are representative for operating conditions, and it is for the Master to
either compare his actual condition with a similar in the Stability Booklet or use a Simplified Stability


                                                           T1
Calculation to estimate the stability of an actual condition of the vessel.


When simplified stability calculations are performed, the master should be aware of the influence of free surface
moments. Since the loading conditions in this booklet are calculated with actual free surface moments (at each
heeling angle), small deviation from the simplified calculations can NOT be prevented.
                                                      ef
Any loading condition calculated by the master must comply with the limiting GM-curves.


NOTE :
                                                   rR
BEFORE E.G. CARRYING HEAVY DECK LOADS AND PERFORMING HEAVY ANCHOR HANDLING, CRANE OPERATION
OR ANY OTHER HEAVY OPERATION, IF APPLICABLE, WHICH EXPECTED TO HAVE A SEVERE EFFECT ON THE VESSEL STABILITY,

                                               tte
APPROPRIATE CALCULATIONS HAVE TO BE DONE TO ENSURE THAT THE OPERATIONAL CONDITIONS FULFILS THE STABILITY CRITERIA.



6.3 FREE SURFACE HANDLING
                                              Le
Provided a tank is completely filled with liquid, no movement of the liquid is possible and the effect on the
ships stability is precisely the same as if the tank contained solid material.


                                       e
Immediately a quantity of the liquid is withdrawn from the tank the situation changes completely and the
stability of the ship is adversely affected by what is know as the FREE SURFACE EFFECT. This adverse effects on
                                  or
the stability is referred to as a loss in GM or as a virtual rise in VCG and is calculated as follows:



                            ap
                      ng      GM Reduction [m] =
                                                     Sum of free surface moments [tm]
                                                                  Displacement [t]
                 Si
           S
Tanks with filling levels fixed (e.g. liquid cargo, water ballast). The free surface correction should be

    AB
determined for the actual/real filling level to be used in each tank.


Tanks with filling levels variable (e.g. consumable liquids such as fuel oil, diesel oil, and fresh water, and
also liquid cargo and water ballast during liquid transfer operations). The free surface correction should be the
maximum value attainable between the filling limits envisaged for each tank, consistent with any operating
 e
instructions.


Se
In calculating the free surface effects in tanks containing consumable liquids, it should be assumed that for


      © 201 5 Ulstein Design & Solutions AS
U10747                                            INSTRUCTIONS FOR MASTER                         2016-03-09
ULSTEIN GROUP
USER AF
                                                                                                  15:28
                                                                                                  Page 16
                                                                                                                 6
                                                                                                            01
each type of liquid at least one transverse pair or a single centreline tank has a free surface and the tank or
combination of tanks taken into account should be those where the effect of free surfaces is the greatest.

                                                                                                     -2
Where water ballast tanks, including anti-rolling tanks and anti-heeling tanks, are to be filled or discharged
during the course of a voyage, the free surface effects should be calculated to take account of the most onerous
transitory stage relating to such operations.
                                                                                                  PR
For vessels engaged in liquid transfer operations, the free surface corrections at any stage of the liquid
transfer operations may be determined in accordance with the filling level in each tank at that stage of the
transfer operation.
                                                                                           -A
NOTE: The free surface effects of all slack tanks should be taken into account in both the arrival and the
departure conditions.
                                                                                       04
NOTE: When it is intended to introduce or discharge ballast water during a voyage the Master should, prior to
departure, ensure that the required stability criteria will be maintained at all times.


                                                                                 ed
Due to the loss of stability by partially filled tanks it is strictly recommended that free surfaces should be
kept to the minimum. If possible, only one center tank/tank pair of each kind of liquid should have a free
surface. As much as practical the tanks with altering content between departure and arrival with largest free
                                                                              at
surface effect should be emptied first. This is in order to avoid large free surfaces as soon as possible during
the voyage. Loading conditions within this document are following the same principle as far as practical.

                                                                            D
Free surface values for all filling levels can be found in the TANK CAPACITY TABLES.



                                                                       74
The FREE SURFACE MOMENTS used in simplified stability calculations (Form1, Form2 and Form3) is the moment of
inertia of the actual tank (m4) multiplied with the specific gravity of the liquid (t/m3). Maximum values for
moment of inertia, given on tank plan drawing could be used as conservative way of maintaining the vessels
stability.



6.4 DECK CARGO
                                                                  91
                                                              49
When loading deck cargo, attention should be paid to the need for maintaining freeboard at the stern with regard
to the safety of the crew working on deck, and also to the adverse effect of trim by stern has on the stability


                                                         T1
of the vessel. the vessel should not be operated at a trim exceeding the values of the min. GM curves. In
addition it should be ensured that the stern trim limitation according to the rules is always enforced.


All doors, hatches and other openings onto exposed cargo deck should be kept closed and secured at sea (except
for access) and it should be ensured that the disposition of the deck cargo does not impede the operation of
these fittings.                                     ef
                                                  rR
When loading deck cargoes, care should be taken to avoid any obstruction of the freeing ports or areas necessary
for the drainage of pipe stowage positions.


When pipe deck cargoes (or other cargoes liable to provide a temporary trap for water) are carried, adequate


                                              tte
areas should be provided between adjacent stowage racks and also between the vessels structure and stowage racks
to ensure free drainage of the pipe stowage positions. Such areas should be in excess of the freeing port area
provided.



                                             Le
When pipes are carried on deck, a volume of entrapped water should be assumed. The centre of gravity of this
entrapped water should be assumed to be at a height above the cargo deck equal to one half the height to the top
of the (pipe) deck cargo. A suitable allowance should also be made where other deck cargoes which may trap water
are carried.
                                      e
The effect of the weight of this trapped water on the vertical centre of gravity and trim of vessel must be taken
into account.                    or
                           ap
The weight of this water is included in the cargo dead-weight permitted by the position of the Load Line Mark.


The minimum GM limitations should not be exceeded and should include an allowance for the effect of entrapped
water in deck cargoes in the total VCG for the relevant conditions.

                     ng
When cargo is discharged at sea, great care must be taken to maintain the vessel in a stable condition during the
discharging operation. Attention should be paid to the trimming of the vessel during unloading.

                Si
- Cargo should be unloaded from the top, i.e. deck cargo should be discharged (heaviest items first) before any
underdeck cargo.


            S
- It should be noted that when liquid cargo is to be discharged, as soon as pumping is commenced a full free
surface will exist in those tanks being pumped and the effect this has on the stability of the vessel taken into

    AB
account.


- The loading pattern of cargo should be such that the freeboard at plimsoll marks is at least 1.3 metres.


- Tanks containing slack liquids should be kept to a minimum.
 e
Se
- Necessary ballasting should be carried out before taking on cargo at sea.

                                                                                                                  01
 6.5 ICING
 If the vessel is engaged in waters, where the possibility of top-side icing may occur, then the Master should
                                                                                                               -2
                                                                                                      PR
 take such action as deemed necessary either to remove this ice, or at least, keep it to a minimum, bearing in
 mind that this top-side icing will adversely affect the stability of the vessel.


 Ice formation may also occur in conditions of snowfall, sea fog (including arctic sea smoke), a drastic fall


                                                                                                     -A
 in ambient temperature, as well as from the freezing of drops of rain on impact with the vessel's structure.
 Ice formation may sometimes be caused or accentuated by water shipped on board and retained on deck.



                                                                                               04
 Intensive ice formation generally occurs on stem, bulwark and bulwark rail, front walls of superstructures and
 deck-houses, hawse holes, anchors, deck gear, forecastle deck and upper deck, freeing ports, aerials, stays,
 shrouds, masts and spars.



                                                                                         ed
 The most intensive ice formation takes place when wind and sea come from ahead. In beam and quartering winds,
 ice accumulates quicker on the windward side of the vessel, thus leading to a constant list which is extremely
 dangerous.


 Consequences of the ice accretion negatively influencing vessel seaworthiness:        at
 1. an increase in the weight of the vessel due to accumulation of ice on the vessel's surfaces which causes
 the reduction of freeboard and buoyancy
                                                                                    D
 2. a rise of the vessel's centre of gravity due to the high location of ice on the vessel's structures with
 corresponding reduction in the level of stability;
                                                                            74
 3. an increase of windage area due to ice formation on the upper parts of the vessel and hence an increase in
 the heeling moment due to the action of the wind


                                                                       91
 4. a change of trim due to uneven distribution of ice along the vessel's length;
 5. the development of a constant list due to uneven distribution of ice across the breadth of the vessel and
 6. impairment of the maneuverability and reduction of the speed of the vessel.



 6.6 DOCKING
                                                                   49
                                                          T1
 When docking the vessel, as much water ballast as possible should be removed. Fuel oil and fresh water should
 be kept to a minimum. Deck cargo or any other cargo should be removed or to kept at bare minimum. This to
 avoid damages to hull in bottom of the vessel.


                                                     ef
 Regarding location of supports and loading condition details for docking see DOCKING PLAN drawing.

6.9 WATERTIGHT INTEGRITY
                                                                                                           01
                                                                                                     -2
The stability calculations are based upon the geometric definition of the hull with relevant appendages. The
following definitions are used through the calculations:
STABHULL Geometric definition for the intact stability calculations.
DAMHULL Geometric definition for the damage stability calculations.
STABHULL Geometric definition for the hydrostatic tables.
                                                                                               PR
                                                                                           -A
The main difference of the above definitions is the above waterline volumes. Wheather or not such a volume should
be included in the buoyancy/stability calculations depends on its watertight integrity.
The requirements due to immersion angles of relevant openings depends on the opening type. The NAPA program has
four different opening types:
- UNPROTECTED
- WEATHERTIGHT
                                                                                      04
- WATERTIGHT


The different opening types are handled in the following way:                   ed
UNPROTECTED:
                                                                             at
Unprotected openings are taken into account in all calculations, lists and plots, wherever openings are
referenced.


WEATHERTIGHT:                                                               D
Weathertight openings do not restrict the calculation of the GZ curve and area calculations, but may not be
submerged in the floating position.


WATERTIGHT:
                                                                         74
Watertight openings are ignored in all calculations. These openings appear only in some lists and as additional
information.
                                                                  91
The program follows the underlying logic in taking relevant openings into account.
The opening is taken into account if:
- It leads from the sea to an undamaged compartment.          49
- It leads from a damaged compartment to an undamaged compartment.
- Data about connection is missing (no record CONNECT)
The opening is ignored if:
- It connects damaged compartments.
                                                         T1
- It connects undamaged compartments.
- It leads from the sea to a damaged compartment.
                                                    ef
You can find list of openings used in the calculations in accordance with the relevant criterias in this chapter.

6.10 PIPECARGOS ON DECK - EFFECT OF ENTRAPPED WATER
                                                                                                            01
                                                                                                     -2
When pipes are carried on deck, a quantity of water has to be assumed to be trapped in and around the pipes,
equal to a certain percentage of the net volume of the pipe deck cargo.


                                                                                                  PR
The net volume should be taken as the internal volume of the pipes plus the volume between the pipes. The
percentage of the net volume used to obtain the quantity of trapped water is based on the freeboard amidships, as
follows,


- 30 % if the summer freeboard amidships to the main deck is equal to or less than 0.015*L.   -A
                                                                                         04
- 10 % if the summer freeboard amidships to the main deck is equal to or greater than 0.03*L.


- For intermediate values of the freeboard amidships, the percentage may be obtained by linear interpolation. For
this vessel the value is 28.2 %.

6.11 SPECIAL CONSIDERATIONS USING PASSIVE ROLL REDUCTION TANKS
                                                                                                            01
ROLL REDUCTION TANK(S) MUST NOT BE USED IN ANY HEAVY OPERATIONS OR HEAVY WEATHER CONDITIONS!!!       -2
               Not part of ABS review (page 21-24)
                                                                                                  PR
This vessel is equipped with an Ulstein Passive Roll Reduction System designed and tested by Marintek, and a copy
of the results in booklet form has been supplied to the vessel. The master should refer to this booklet for
operation information. Please read this chapter carefully. In all loading conditions where the roll reduction
tank(s) are included, the tank(s) should be filled to their working level and the full free surface loss taken
into account when assessing the vessels stability.
                                                                                           -A
The working level of the tanks varies with the displacement of the vessel and is found within this chapter.


                                                                                      04
Filling and/or discharging of the tank(s) is through the ballast/fire pumps situated in engine room. To eliminate
the free surface loss when stability is critical the time to fill or empty the tanks from working level should be
as short as possible.



                                                                                  ed
The limitations on use of roll-reduction tanks should be observed. When the tanks are in use, the FREE SURFACE
EFFECT should be taken into account in the calculations.


Any loading condition calculated by the master must comply with the limiting GM-curves, which can be found in
                                                                             at
Chapter 8 of this stability manual. If the actual GM (corrected for FREE SURFACE) is on or above the minimum GM
value the stability of the vessel is satisfactory.

                                                                            D
Free surface values for all filling levels can be found in the Chapter 11 TANK CAPACITY TABLES.



                                                                          74
Due to the shape of a passive roll reduction tank, its use reduces the GM significantly and should be considered
specially regarding the vessels stability.


On general basis it is the designers advice that due to possible sudden changes in weather during operation,

                                                                  91
possible obstructions on crane loads or anchor loads, and possible heavier loads than anticipated, roll reduction
tanks should not be used during operation. This to preserve stability reserves.



                                                              49
Roll reduction tanks must neither be used in any conditions with an initial GM0 (prior to free surface
correction) close to minimum allowed GM.




                                                         T1
NOTE: BEFORE CARRYING HEAVY DECK LOADS AND PERFORMING HEAVY ANCHOR HANDLING, CRANE OPERATION AND ANY OTHER HEAVY
OPERATION EXPECTED TO HAVE A SEVERE EFFECT ON THE VESSEL, SPECIAL STABILITY CALCULATIONS HAS TO BE DONE TO ENSURE
THAT THE CONDITION FULFILS THE STABILITY CRITERION.


In case of grounding, collision or other outside influence on the vessel, the tank must be emptied immediately.
                                                     ef
When it is intended to introduce or discharge ballast water during a voyage the Master should, prior to


                                                  rR
departure, ensure that the required stability criteria will be maintained at all times.

Find the period of rolling Tr by:             tte

                                      e
level of liquid for any period of rolling.


                                 or

                           ap

ballasting.


In all loading conditions where the stabilizing tanks are included, the tanks should be filled to their working

                     ng
level and the full free surface loss taken into account when assessing the vessels stability.


Filling and/or discharging of the ballast tanks is through the vessels fire/ballast pumps. To eliminate the free

                Si
surface loss when stability is critical the time to fill or empty the tanks from working level should be as short
as possible.


The tank will have a complete free surface as ballasting commences, or as soon pumping starts from a full tank.
            S

    AB
full. Those tanks which are supposed to be dry should be completely dry.


The free surface will adversely effect the stability of the vessel before any benefit can be assumed by the
weight of the ballast water taken onboard. Provided a tank is completely filled with liquid, no movement of the
liquid is possible and the effect on the ships stability is precisely the same as if the tank contained solid
 e

6.11.2 CONDITIONS WHICH INFLUENCE THE FUNCTIONALITY OF THE SYSTEM                              PR
Too much or too little liquid reduces effect.
                                                                                           -A
When the rolling periods are very short, it may happen that the liquid just splashes around without any effect.


                                                                                      04
If the tank is placed fairly high (above the centre of gravity), one solution may be to fill it up. This will
give a longer, and more agreeable period of rolling.


This effect is not caused by the tank as such, but the fact that placing the weight higher, reduces an extremely


                                                                                 ed
good stability. Changing ballast from tanks placed low in the vessel, to tanks higher up will enhance this
effect.


Increased KG, decreased GM implies longer rolling period.
                                                                             at
Extremely long periods of rolling indicates that the stability is unsatisfactory (low GM). A stability check can

                                                                            D
be done by comparing the actual metacentric height GM with the minimum GM. Minimum GM is the least metacentric
height allowed by the authorities on a given displacement.



                                                                          74
The consideration of comfortable motion and better working conditions for the crew is important, but MUST NOT
under any circumstances put the ships stability aside.


Note how the use of these tanks dramatically decreases the loads one can put onto the vessel, i.e. crane loads,
anchorhandling loads, deck loads etc.

Deterministic damage stability criteria description :
                                                                                                            01
*** MSC.335[90]
This vessel should comply with damage stability criteria as stated in IMO MSC.335(90) AMMENDMENTS TO THE
GUIDELINES FOR THE DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION OF OFFSHORE SUPPLY VESSELS, 2006. (RESOLUTION MSC.235(82))
                                                                                                        -2
                                                                                                 PR
Damage should be assumed to occur anywhere in the vessel's length between transverse watertight bulkheads.
The longitudinal extent of damage should be assumed for vessels with the length (L) greater than 43 m, and
less than 80 m:3 m plus 3% of the vessel's length. For those with length (L) not greater than 43 m, 10% of the
vessel's length and for those with length from 80 to 100 m: 1/3 L**2/3.
For this vessel the longitudinal extent of damage of 5.388 m
was calculated.
                                                                                           -A
                                                                                       04
The vertical extent of damage should be assumed from the underside of the cargo deck, or the continuation
thereof, for the full depth of the vessel.



                                                                                  ed
The transverse extent of damage should be assumed as 760 mm for vessels with length less than 80 m and
B/20, but not less than 760 m for vessels with length from 80 to 100 m.
The transverse extent should be measured inboard from the side of the vessel perpendicularly to the
centerline at the level of the summer load waterline.
                                                                                  at
If pipes, ducts or tunnels are situated within the assumed extent of damage, arrangements should be made

                                                                                  D
to ensure that progressive flooding cannot thereby extend to compartments other than those assumed to be
floodable for each case of damage.



                                                                             74
If a damage of a lesser extent than that specified above results in a more severe condition,
such lesser extent should be assumed. Where a transverse watertight bulkhead is located within the transverse
extent of assumed damage and is stepped in way of a double bottom or side tank by more than 3.05 m, the
double bottom or side tanks adjacent to the stepped portion of the transverse watertight bulkhead should be
considered as flooded simultaneously.
****
                                                                        91
**** V.PROGR.A469
                                                                       49
The final waterline, taking into account sinkage, heel and trim, should be below lower edge of any opening
through which progressive flooding may take place. Such openings should include airpipes and those which are


                                                               T1
capable of being closed by means of watertight doors or hatch covers and may exclude those openings closed
by means of watertight manhole covers and flush scuttles, small watertight cargo tank hatch covers which
maintain the high integrity of the deck, remotely operated sliding doors and side scuttles of the nonopening
type.

**** V.MAXHEEL.A469
                                                          ef
                                                     rR
In the final stage of flooding, the angle of heel due to unsymmetrical flooding should not exceed 15 degrees.
This angle may be increased up to 17 degrees if no deck immersion occurs.

**** V.RANGE.A469
                                                 tte
The stability in the final stage of flooding should be investigated and may be regarded as sufficient if the
righting lever curve has at least a range of 20 degrees beyond the position of equilibrium. Unprotected
openings should not become immersed at an angle of heel within the prescribed minimum range of residual

                                                Le
stability unless the space in question has been included as a floodable space in calculations for damage
stability.

                                    or

with a maximum residual righting lever of at least 100 mm within this range. Unprotected openings should not

space in question has been included as a floodable space in calculations for damage stability.

                                                                                                                      01
GENERAL
                                                                                                               -2
The ability of a ship to withstand the combined effects of beam wind and rolling should be
demonstrated for each standard condition of loading, with reference to the figure as follows:               PR
The ship is subjected to a steady wind pressure acting perpendicular to the ships centreline which
result in a steady wind heeling lever (Lw1).
                                                                                                   -A
From the resultant angle of equilibrium (Theta0) the ship is assumed to roll owing to wave action to


                                                                                          04
an angle of roll (Theta1) to windward. Attention should be paid to the effect of steady wind so that
excessive resultant angles of heel are avoided:


The angle of heel under action of steady wind (Theta0) should be limited to a certain angle to the


                                                                                      ed
satisfaction of the Administration. As a guide, 16 degrees or 80% of the angle of deck edge
immersion, whichever is less, is suggested.


The ship is then subjected to a gust wind pressure which results in a gust wind heeling lever (Lw2).
Under these circumstances, area B should be equal to or greater than area A.         at
Proper free surface effects should be accounted for in the standard conditions of loading.

7 MANUAL DETERMINATION OF STABILITY ON BOARD
                                                                                                            01
7.1 GENERAL                                                                                             -2
                                                                                               PR
Using the stability forms (form1, form2 and form3) together with the tank plan/tank capacities hydrostatic tables
and cross-curves it is possible to carry out stability calculations for different loading conditions compared
with the loading conditions calculated in advance.



                                                                                              -A
The documents are composed in such a way that the stability calculations may be carried out schematically.


The tables contain all necessary basic data for the calculations which have to be logged in form1, form2 and
form3.


THE FOLLOWING TABLES AND FORMS ARE USED IN THE CALCULATIONS
                                                                                          04
- Drawing tank plan (chap. 13)
- Tank capacities (chap. 11)
- Tables of hydrostatics (chap. 10)
                                                                                         ed
- Cross curves of stability (chap. 9)
- Form1 : Blank form calculation of loaded ship (chap. 7)
- Form2 : Blank form hydrostatic values (chap. 7)
                                                                                   at
- Form3 : Blank form GZ-curve (chap. 7)


INSTRUCTIONS FOR STABILITY CALCULATIONS
                                                                                D
                                                                          74
To get correct result of these calculations it is recommended to read the instructions very carefully and follow
them step by step.



7.2 CALCULATION OF LOADED SHIP - FORM1                               91
                                                                 49
- Enter the individual weights (light ship, crew and provisions, tank capacities, cargo and miscellaneous
weights) in the column WEIGHT.




                                                            T1
- Ascertain the vertical centre of gravity above baseline of the individual weights and enter same in the column
VCG.


- Multiply the individual weight by the corresponding vertical centre of gravity. Enter in column MV.


                                                         ef
- Add the individual weights. Enter in column TOTAL SUM (1).




                                                     rR
- Add the vertical moments. Enter in column TOTAL SUM (3).


- Divide (3) / (1) = (6) = VCG. Enter into position VCG (6).




                                                 tte
VCG = Vertical centre of gravity above baseline of the loaded vessel.


NOTE:


                                                Le
The next four items are required only to be considered if a trim calculation is to be carried out.


- Ascertain the longitudinal centers of gravity of the individual weights and enter same in column LCG.


                                         e
- Multiply the individual weight by the corresponding longitudinal centre of gravity. Enter in column ML.


                                    or
- Add the longitudinal moments. Enter in column TOTAL SUM (2).



                              ap
- Divide (2) / (1) = (5) = LCG. Enter into position LCG (5).


LCG = longitudinal centre of gravity of the loaded vessel measured from AP.


                        ng

                   Si

             S

INFLUENCE OF FREE SURFACES                                                                                    01
                                                                                                        -2
For partially filled consumable tanks the value FSM (Moment of free surface) of drawing TANK PLAN to be applied
to FORM1 column FSM or to be taken form the capacity tables.


- Enter the density for all partially filled tanks into FORM1 column RHO.
                                                                                               PR
- Get the moment of inertia IT for the actual tank from drawing TANK PLAN or from the capacity tables.



                                                                                             -A

- Divide (4) / (1) = (7) = dGM.                                                          04
dGM = loss of stability due to free surface effect.

7.4 GZ-CURVE - FORM3
                                                               49
CALCULATION OF GM                                         T1
The value of KMT and cross curve data calculated in FORM2 are to be applied to calculation of lever arm curve
(GZ-curve) in FORM3:
                                                       ef
- Transfer the values of displacement, LCG, VCG and dGM calculated in FORM1 to the position (1) (5) (6) and (7)
of FORM2 respectively.

                                                   rR
- Transfer the value of KMT from FORM2 column(21) first row to FORM3 position (22).




                                               tte
- Transfer the KN-values from FORM2 column(21) to the corresponding heeling angles in FORM3 row(27).


- Subtract (22) - (6) = (23) = GM0. Enter into FORM3 position (23).



                                              Le
- Subtract (23) - (7) = (24) = GM. Enter into FORM3 position (24).


- Add (6) + (7) = (25). Enter into FORM3 position (25).



GM0 = Initial metacentric height
                                       e
                                  or
GM = Metacentric height corrected for free surface effect.
KG = Centre of gravity for loaded ship corrected for free surface effect.


                            ap
KG is measured from the baseline.
GM and GM0 is measured from the centre of gravity for loaded ship.


                      ng
DRAWING OF LEVER ARM CURVE (GZ)

Calculation of table for the righting lever arm (GZ) :

                 Si
- Multiply each value in row(26) with the value of KG(25), and enter results in row (28).


- For each heeling angle subtract (27) - (28) = (29) = GZ, and enter results in row (29).
           S
    AB
Drawing the lever arm curve:


- Offset a point on the dashed line marked GM in such way that the point is corresponding with the value of
GM(24) on the righting lever axis.

 e
- Draw a straight line from this point to the origin of the chart diagram.


Se
- Tag the points listed in row(29) into the chart diagram.

7.5 COMPLIANCE WITH STABILITY CRITERIA
                                                                                                                                                      01
7.5.1 GENERAL
                                                                                                                                               -2
In order to carry out a stability check for the actual loading condition the Master should follow one of the
following instructions :
                                                                                                                                            PR
- Check against MINGM-curve
- Check against the loading conditions calculated in advance
- Check against relevant criteria (Both intact and damage criteria !)
                                                                                                                                  -A
Instructions for calculation of GM and drawing of GZ-curve are given in chapter 7. It is of great importance for
the stability that the ship is balanced transversely, giving zero heeling moment in all conditions.
                                                                                                                             04
To calculate the heeling moment due to loaded ship :                                                                        ed
- For every tank and mass load :
Heeling moment = Weight of tank or mass multiplied with the transverse centre of gravity TCG with sign (Weight
and TCG given in ch. 2 or app. 3).
                                                                                                                       at
- For loaded ship: Heeling moment = sum of heeling moments calculated above.                                        D
                                                                                                               74
If the GZ-curve is calculated (ch. 7) it is possible to check the stability against relevant stability criteria.
NOTE: When carrying heavy deck loads, special stability calculations has to be done to ensure that the condition
fulfils the stability criterion.




7.5.2 CHECK AGAINST MINIMUM GM CURVE
                                                                                                              91
                                                                                                     49
Calculation of GM using standard forms is described in chapter 7. The calculated GM is compared to the
MINGM-curve as shown below. If the actual GM (corrected for free surface) is on or above the minimum GM value the
stability of the vessel is satisfactory.

7.5.3 CALCULATION OF AREA BELOW GZ-CURVE
                                                                                                              01
                                                                                                       -2
In order to compare the actual GZ-curve against stability criteria it is necessary to calculate the area below
the GZ-curve.


                                                                                               PR
On the following page an example showing how to calculate the area below 40 degrees is described.



To calculate the area up to DELTA degrees do following :


- Calculate CI = Common angle in interval = DELTA / 8
                                                                                           -A
- Replace column I with angles in interval CI, i.e. 0*CI , 1*CI, 2*CI ... 8*CI.        04
- Read off the GZ-values at given angles of heel, and enter same into column III.


                                                                                      ed
- For each angle of heel multiply column II and column III, and enter the result into column IV.


- Calculate the sum of column IV and enter into position SUM IV =....


- Calculate the area by use of the formula:
                                                                                at
AREA = (CI/3) * (SUM IV) * 0.01745 = ............. meter radians             D
If you want the area between 30 and 40 degrees, do following :
                                                                       74
                                                                  91
- Use the instructions above to calculate the area for DELTA = 30 deg


- Use the same procedure for DELTA = 40 degrees.

                                                              49
- Area between 30 and 40 degrees is given by: AREA40-30 = AREA40 - AREA30 = ......

8.1 INTERPOLATION BETWEEN CURVES
                                                                                                            -2
Please follow the checklist below being sure of using the curves correctly:                           PR
1. Calculate the GM using standard forms described in chapter 8.


2. Make sure the calculated GM is corrected for free surfaces.
                                                                                                     -A
3. Make sure the ship is transversely balanced giving zero heeling moment.                          04
4. If the actual trim is between the values of trim listed, the maximum GM-value for the nearest trim values may
be used.


OR:
                                                                                                ed
Use the interpolation formula below to calculate the minimum GM for the actual trim.        at
                                                                                            D
5. If the minimum GM-value is LESS THAN the actual GM (corrected for free surfaces) the stability of the vessel
is satisfactory.



                                                                                    74
                                     MinGM [m] = GM1 +
                                                                                 91
                                                                     ( GM2 - GM1 ) * ( TR - TR1 )
                                                                            ( TR2 - TR1 )
                                                                           49
                                                                      T1
TR1, TR2 and TR are trim values LOW, HIGH and ACTUAL respectively.
GM1 and GM2 are minGM corresponding to trim values TR1 and TR2.
TR1 and TR2 have to be chosen in such way giving TR2>TR>TR1.         ef
                                                           rR
Explanation of symbols used in GM LIMIT TABLES :
T - draught
IGMLIM - GM limit values for intact stability
                                                     tte
ICRLIM - intact criteria limiting the GM for corresponding GM limit value

                                                Le
ITEXT - text describing the corresponding intact criteria
GMLIM - overall resulting GM limit value for corresponding draught


DGMLIM - GM limit values for deterministic damage stability
                                          e
DCRLIM - deterministic damage criteria limiting the GM for corresponding GM limit value
DTEXT - text describing the corresponding deterministic damage criteria

                                                                                                                    01
This chapter contains detailed documentation of the loading conditions. The below briefly listed loading
conditions are documented on the next pages for both intact and damage stability. The calculation of
                                                                                                                -2
the stability curve and the metacentric height, GM, take the actual floating position into account.
Therefore, small deviation to manual calculations can NOT be prevented.                                  PR
The real free surface moment is calculated for the tanks at their actual filling. The correction for


                                                                                                    -A
different heeling angles is got by calculating the real new center of gravity for the load in the heeled
tank. The correction for the initial GM is got by calculating the real moment of inertia for the
surface in the tank.
                                                                                                           free



                                                                                                 04
Please, refer to the chapter INSTRUCTIONS FOR MASTER for further details of the calculation methods.
